analysis.method: For three-value Counts=[1,8,1] distributions, p25/p50/p75 lie inside the central bin, not at global extrema. Infer candidate index as round(log(native_p50)/log(1.1)-0.5). Compare only in a throwaway Python calculation with floor(log(input)/log(1.1)) and current geometric interpolation formula. This is not execution of the Go implementation and is not an independent native oracle.

analysis_notes: Account verified once by STS before any publication. The first query was rejected as an invalid statistic; the next successful query proved all requested timestamps initially absent. One publication then one bounded visibility read exposed p50 at all 36 timestamps and 4405 statistic values; omissions remain exactly as returned.

No bin-index mismatch was observed against the Python evaluation of the current generic logarithmic formula across 32 unclipped cases. This does not establish exact Go math.Log/math.Pow parity or universality.

Native distinguishes 1.21 (p50 1.153689732987167; inferred bin 1) from adjacent float 1.2100000000000002 (p50 1.2690587062858836; inferred bin 2). Likewise 1.3310000000000002 remains in inferred bin 2 while binary-base pow 1.3310000000000004 is in inferred bin 3. Decimal edge labels must not be treated as exact float thresholds.

For powers 7 and 10, nominal decimal edges and their immediate nextups remain below the observed transition reached by binary-base 1.1**n values. For power -3, 1.1**-3=0.7513148009015775 falls in inferred bin -4, while decimal-rounded nextdown 0.7513148009015777 is already in bin -3. These observations support sensitivity to binary floating-point evaluation; they do not distinguish native logarithm rounding from its hidden boundary representation.

Equivalent JSON decimal spellings of 1.1 and 1.21 produced identical presence and values for all 137 queried statistics. The CLI parses these JSON numerals into the same binary64 double before sending; this cannot prove native wire-lexeme invariance.

Clipped-minimum 1.21 shows p50 1.2100000000000002 although the supplied minimum is 1.21; TC(:1.2100)=0 and TC(1.2100:)=9. Clipped-maximum 1.21 instead has p50 1.1468377629586062, TC(:1.2100)=9 and TC(1.2100:)=0. Narrow TC(1.2099:1.2101) is 8 versus 0.00727272727272648, respectively. These are observed distinctions between full logarithmic membership and extrema-clipped interpolation.

All four spelling cases used the indicated original decimal JSON lexeme through --cli-input-json; the input mapping retains parsed numeric values. Other values used standard round-trip Python JSON float serialization.

Main added nine independent read-only precision requests after the agent capture, preserving individual native validation results rather than inferring one universal rule from the initial compound request.

Actual stackd CLI replay matched all 4405 matrix values at relative tolerance 1e-8, including exact-adjacent input distinctions. The long-decimal query was incorrectly accepted locally; subsequent single-stat native probes establish a ten-decimal-place limit for percentile, fixed/percentage trim, rank and short winsor forms, including trailing zeros.
limitations: Finite ordinary-magnitude sample matrix, powers -3,-1,0,1,2,3,7,10 only; no extreme magnitudes, negative values, zero counts, or multi-writer collision testing.

The native request containing TC(:0.7513148009015778) was rejected at that statistic; the returned message does not prove an exact decimal-digit limit. A replacement matrix with four-decimal fixed cutoffs succeeded. Adjacent-double fixed cutoffs therefore were not observed; adjacent metric inputs and percentile outputs were observed.

No Go source, tests, docs, existing fixture, probe helper, or test harness changed; no validation/build/test commands executed. Python comparison remains an analysis-only approximation of the source formula.
No further polling after all p50 points became visible; individual omitted fixed-trim results are native observations at one retrieval time, not claims of permanent absence.

Native logarithm implementation, exact hidden bin thresholds and ULP-level bin-edge construction remain unknown. Small interpolation differences from Python predictions must not be overwritten with local values.
